content:
The pen lies on the blotter, angled toward you the way Krail aligns everything—documents, cutlery, people. Its nib is clean. The approval space on the punishment order stays blank, a pale rectangle exactly the size of a name.

"young lord." Krail's voice stays level, dry as ledger paper. "The household requires a decision before the evening inventory. The fire is extinguished. The confession is recorded. All that remains is the authorization." He does not tap the page. He does not need to. His grey eyes rest on you with the patient attention of a man who has watched two older children sign worse things.

Across the room, Liora's breath comes too fast. She stands half a step in front of her mother, as if that could shield either of them, and her reddish-brown eyes keep darting from the order to your face. Soot still streaks one cheek. Her injured palm is curled against her skirt, and every time she shifts her weight, the red layers of her hair flash through the black like something catching light.

"young lord, I—" she starts, and Elise's good hand closes gently on her shoulder.

"Hush, love." Elise's voice is steadier than her hands. She turns to you, smooths her apron out of habit, and holds her posture straight despite the bandage on her left forearm, brown-stained at its center. "I'll not beg, young lord. My daughter took my keys without my knowing and caused the fire through her own clumsiness. That's hers to answer for. I answer for my wing and my keys, no more. I did not give permission, and I'll swear that before any priest you name." Her mouth tightens. "But I'll say this once. We put the fire out ourselves before the bucket lines arrived. We carried each other out. Whatever the order says, we're not untended yet only because no one has looked at us."

Beside you, Isolde has not moved. Her white hair sits in clean lines against her black collar; her hands rest folded at her apron. When she speaks, her voice is flat and precise, each word set down like a ledger entry. "young lord, confirming my earlier report. The physician in the east wing has attended no one from this room. Elise Fen's bandage has not been changed since it was applied by another maid. Liora Fen's burn is untreated. Estimated delay since the fire: more than two hours." She pauses, then adds, without any change of tone: "I observed no attempt to obtain treatment."

Krail's jaw does not tighten, but something in his stillness does. "Medical attention can follow authorization," he says. "The order provides for it. Discipline first, then the physician. That is the household's established sequence, young lord, and the duke has never found fault with it."

From the passage beyond the door comes a small sound—the creak of a floorboard under a weight that shifts, then stills. Magerrett, listening. Farther down the corridor, fainter, another sound that might be a door easing shut.

Krail lets the silence sit. Then, in the tone of a man concluding a routine transaction, he slides the order a half-inch closer to you and picks up the pen, holding it out across the desk, grip first.

"The duke returns after sunset," he says. "He will ask what was decided in his absence. I would prefer to tell him the household functioned as it should." His thin lips flatten into something that is almost courtesy. "Or, if the young lord prefers, the matter can wait until he returns—but the prisoners remain detained either way, and untreated wounds have a way of becoming someone's fault by morning."

He holds the pen out. Waits.

Liora's eyes are on your hand. Elise's are on your face. Isolde watches the pen itself, yellow eyes tracking it the way she tracks anything that might move.
